findings.title: Wrong binding semantics
findings.body:
A Cloudflare `secrets_store` binding points at one secret, and the Worker reads it with `env.X.get()` (no arguments). This code sets `secret_name` to the binding name, so `bindings: { SECRETS: store }` binds a secret literally named `SECRETS`. That secret usually doesn't exist in the store.

It also contradicts the `SecretsStoreBinding.get(secretName)` type and the documented `env.SECRETS.get("API_KEY")` usage, which treat the binding as a whole-store accessor. Worker code following the docs will fail at runtime. Either bind one secret per entry in `secrets`, or let the user specify which secret to bind.

findings.title: Update re-creates secrets
findings.body:
In the update phase, `insertSecrets` POSTs every secret in `props.secrets` to the create endpoint, including secrets that already exist in the store. The only cleanup beforehand is deleting removed names.

This affects any update where a secret is unchanged or only its value changes. Creating an already-existing secret name will likely be rejected, so the update throws, and changed values are never applied.

The same applies to the adopt path when the adopted store already holds some of the secrets. Existing secrets should be updated (PATCH), or deleted and then re-created.

findings.title: Scope name regression
findings.body:
This PR removes the `describe` block name from the test scope name, so scopes are now named only by `testName`. Two tests with the same name in different `describe` blocks of one file will now share a scope. Their resources and state will collide, and one test's destroy can delete the other's resources.

This change looks unrelated to the Secrets Store feature and silently changes behavior for all existing tests.
